+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+data = duckdb.connect().execute(
+    """
+    SELECT YEAR(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0))::INTEGER AS motorist_deaths,
+           SUM(COALESCE(number_of_cyclist_killed, 0))::INTEGER AS cyclist_deaths
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY 1
+    ORDER BY 1
+    """
+).fetchdf()
+
+years = data["year"].to_numpy()
+motorist = data["motorist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+cyclist = data["cyclist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+
+# Option 1: annual death counts by road-user type, shown as grouped bars.
+data.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.8))
+x = np.arange(len(years))
+width = 0.38
+ax.bar(x - width / 2, motorist, width, label="Motorists", color="#315a8a")
+ax.bar(x + width / 2, cyclist, width, label="Cyclists", color="#e28b36")
+ax.set_xticks(x, years)
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths (people)")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("Motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC by year, 2013–2025")
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.2)
+ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 2: same annual counts, emphasizing their trajectories with lines.
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.8))
+ax.plot(years, motorist, marker="o", linewidth=2.2, label="Motorists", color="#315a8a")
+ax.plot(years, cyclist, marker="o", linewidth=2.2, label="Cyclists", color="#e28b36")
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths (people)")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("Annual motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC, 2013–2025")
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+ax.grid(alpha=0.22)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 3: cyclist deaths relative to motorist deaths, per 100 motorist deaths.
+ratio = cyclist / motorist * 100
+ratio_data = pd.DataFrame(
+    {"year": years, "cyclist_deaths_per_100_motorist_deaths": np.round(ratio, 1)}
+)
+ratio_data.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+gap_data = pd.DataFrame(
+    {"year": years, "motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths": motorist - cyclist}
+)
+# The difference is also retained as plotted data for option 2? No: values_2 is
+# the two plotted series for its lines, matching that chart's actual data.
+data.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.8))
+ax.bar(years, gap_data["motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths"], color="#567b65", width=0.72)
+ax.axhline(0, color="#444444", linewidth=0.8)
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.set_ylabel("More motorist than cyclist deaths (people)")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_title("Annual gap between motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC, 2013–2025")
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.2)
+ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Replace option 3 values with the values actually plotted (annual death gap).
+gap_data.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual deaths among motorists and cyclists",
+            "denominator": "None; counts of reported deaths",
+            "grouping": "Year and road-user type",
+            "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart",
+            "reason": "Side-by-side bars make the yearly absolute difference between the two groups easy to compare.",
+            "probability": 0.38,
+            "answer": "Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; the largest gap was 110 deaths in 2020 (139 vs. 29), and the smallest was 51 in 2019 (82 vs. 31).",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual deaths among motorists and cyclists",
+            "denominator": "None; counts of reported deaths",
+            "grouping": "Year, with separate series for motorists and cyclists",
+            "chart_type": "Two-series line chart",
+            "reason": "Lines emphasize how each group's annual death count changed over time.",
+            "probability": 0.34,
+            "answer": "Motorist deaths peaked at 139 in 2020 and were lowest at 72 in 2016, while cyclist deaths peaked at 31 in both 2019 and 2023 and were lowest at 10 in 2018.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths",
+            "denominator": "None; difference in reported death counts",
+            "grouping": "Year",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart of annual differences",
+            "reason": "The difference directly quantifies how many more motorist than cyclist deaths were recorded each year.",
+            "probability": 0.28,
+            "answer": "Motorist deaths were higher every year, with the annual excess ranging from 51 in 2019 to 110 in 2020; it was 58 in 2025 (81 motorist deaths versus 23 cyclist deaths).",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
*** End Patch
